cues.text: Hello, I’m new in the area and I’d like to join the library please.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: That’s no problem. Let me get an application form. Here we are. Now all we have to do is fill this in and then I’ll get you to sign and you’ll be a member.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Great
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Now then. What’s your full name?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Peter Adrian camden .
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: How do you spell Camden?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: C-A-M-D-E-N
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: C-A-M-D-E-N
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Yes, that’s right.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Right, and what’s your address?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: flat 553 Green street , Finsbury.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Ok. Got that. That’s near here isn’t it?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Yes, just 5 minutes walk.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: What’s the post code?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: 7424.. I..I mean, sorry,   7 4 3 4
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Got that now. Now, can you tell me your date of birth?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: 8th of July, 1976
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: And, what’s your telephone number?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Well, I don’t have a home number but I’ve got a mobile.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: That’ll do fine.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: It’s o six six three four nine eight two seven four six . Did you get that?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Some of it. Can you say it again?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: The code’s 06634 and the number’s then 982 746
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Right. That’s almost it. Now I need some kind of identification to prove where you live. Do you have a driving license or a passport or anything like that?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: I’m afraid that everything I have, has got my old address on it. Do you need it now?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: No, not now, but you won’t be able to take anything out until we see that.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Wait a minute. I’ve got a letter addressed to me here that arrived this morning. Will that do?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Oh yes. That’s a good idea. That will be fine. Let’s look. Ok. Well, that’s that finished.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Could I ask you a few questions? The Council that runs the library is running a survey to find out what kind of books people prefer so that they can direct their buying.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Yeah, no problem.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: OK. So, what type of books do you like?
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Well, I’m very keen on mysteries . You know, when a detective is trying to find out who did the murder .
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Historical novels interest me too. Romance never! My sister loves them but they bore me to tears.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: I quite like books on animals too. I get them out sometimes. Not science fiction either. Too weird.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, I think that’s it then.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Good. Oh, do you charge anything?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: The library is free unless you want to rent out some of our videos or DVDs.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: How much is that?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, we rent videos out for four dollars each and DVDs are six dollars . You must leave us a deposit for $60 of$60 as well. That’s returnable of course.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: I don’t think I’ll get any of those just yet. Can I pay later?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Sure, just give the money in when you’re ready to rent them out.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Well thanks very much. You’ve been very helpful. I might take a book out now for the weekend, if that’s OK?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Go ahead.
cues.speaker: Will

cues.text: Well, goodbye.
cues.speaker: Peter
